FOUR ROUNDS, AND EACH ONE CHANGED EXACTLY ONE THING:
  r1  three concepts, Matrixyl teal fibre — wrong: the concern-to-colour map colours the tiles and banners, not the anatomy
  r2  same three concepts in generic skin colour; Malcolm chose C luma_02
  r3  one concept, front elevation and zoomed, layer stack transcribed off luma_02; leader was C nbp_flash_02
  r4  the damage moved from the right end into the middle, sound tissue at both edges

WHY THIS CANDIDATE. It is the only one of the r4 leaders that satisfies all four things the brief was actually protecting:
  1. The block is sound at BOTH ends and fails through the middle, so the picture has no direction in it and therefore makes no before-and-after claim.
  2. The two sound ends are NOT mirror images — the fibre courses differ left from right, the lobules differ in size and spacing, and the failure zone sits off centre. The mirrored-diptych failure this round was written to prevent did not occur.
  3. The block stays ONE CONTINUOUS PIECE. The middle is thinned, parted and sagging; it is never cut through. A gap top to bottom would read as a wound, which is a far worse claim than a loss of density.
  4. At 100% the parted fibre ends are SOLID and rounded. This is what settled it against nbp_pro_01, whose ends have a visible open bore and read as cut piping rather than fibre — the same fault that appeared on two r3 candidates and was added to the r4 negatives.

All four causes in the copy are legible without a single label: granules crumbling and drifting (collagen degradation), fibres frayed and parted with the ends drawn back (elastin fragmentation), lobules shrunk to small beads with the floor dipping over them (fat pad redistribution), and the surface sinking into a valley over the whole zone — the one part a shopper reads as their own face. Hormonal change is not depicted, because it is a driver and not a visible structure.

SQUARE, 1:1, NON-NEGOTIABLE. The row height in `media-with-text` is set by the master's own aspect: a non-square file stretches the row and makes this block taller than its five siblings. Learned twice on this store in one day — see the key-findings-box memory.

No actives in frame: no spheres, no light shafts, no glints. This block is the damage; the next block on the page, 'The Collagen-Peptide Approach to Firming', is where the repair belongs.
